item.title: `comrak`: CommonMark + GFM compatible Markdown parser and renderer
item.content:encoded:
• comrak: CommonMark + GFM compatible Markdown parser and renderer
    • Recap: convert from a markdown file with the path into HTML in the stdout.
      • really similar to a SSG.
    • Run: 
      comrak $jtb["fm"] | bat -lhtml # for my profiles... could try a readme for a simpler example.
# A variable can contain a file handle. with `miniserve` you can update the file....
# with text editor even.
comrak $jtb["fm"] > ($a = ni -p $env:TEMP -n "edgerun.html" -Force); miniserve $a && rm $a
# hopefully in the future it could be like this.
comrak $jtb["fm"] > ($a = New-TemporaryFile -extension html); msedge $a
      • #cli/option : -o | --output "FILE" will output to a file, thus reduce above kludges. 
        comrak ./README.MD -o ./README.html ; msedge $pwd/README.html # notice msedge cant expand the "." dir.

    • Resolution:

      • you could pipe to a Temp file and let miniserve serve it.
      • #nodejs #cli #pipeline node-bcat: A pipe to browser utility
        • #alternative : How to pipe html into lynx? 
          cat ./a-file-ends-with.html | lynx -stdin
    • Reason:
    • Root:
    • Related:
      • #powershell: Add ability to create a temporary file with a specific extension to New-TemporaryFile · Issue #4215 · PowerShell/PowerShell
      • Does any web browser allow writing to stdout?
    • Rival: cmark CommonMark parsing and rendering library and program in C
      • Recap: to force myself better I shim comrak to cmark — less syllable to look on.
      • Root: soupault
      • Are Feeds - like RSS or Atom feeds - Really worth it for a personal blog? - ~comp - Tildes
